notices.format: Statement of buyer's rights that complies with the FTC notice of cancellation rule; no Colorado wording of its own
notices.support: The statement shall comply with any notice of cancellation or a similar requirement of any trade regulation rule of the federal trade commission that by its terms applies to the home solicitation sale.
notices.summary_row: Form of agreement, statement of buyer's rights (adopts FTC notice)
notices.hold_reason: no prescribed wording; the statute only requires a statement that complies with the FTC notice of cancellation rule

changes.new: Federal for cash sales; state home solicitation covers credit sales only (C.R.S. 5-3-401, official text)
changes.support: 'Home solicitation sale' means a consumer credit sale of goods or services in which the seller or a person acting for the seller personally solicits the sale

changes.new: CDARA 13-20-803.5, 75 days before filing an action (90 days for commercial property)
changes.support: No later than seventy-five days before filing an action against a construction professional, or no later than ninety days before filing the action in the case of a commercial property

changes.new: Reminder 25 to 40 days before renewal, retainable acknowledgment, easy cancellation; a renewal term over one year needs express written consent
changes.support: A renewal term longer than one year needs "express written consent".

changes.new: OFFICIAL text (CRS 2026, olls.info); since February 16, 2026 a consumer includes business customers; no exemption for cleaning or home services
changes.support: No exemption for cleaning or home services appears in subsection (5).

unsure: CO-cancel-credit: Colorado prints no wording of its own (it adopts the FTC notice), so nothing is loaded; the notice also only applies to credit sales, which the builder cannot tell.
The permit-office lien notice (38-22-105.5) is mailed by the permit office, not the contractor, so it was not added as a contract notice.
